ق is a glottal stop and the taa marbuta after و is e: 'ahwe. The nisba adjective agrees in the feminine: 3arabiyye.
ق glottalises: ta'liidi, with long ii and a short final -i for the nisba. Used of traditional dress, food and customs.
Form VIII defective verb, the initial vowel written bare: ishtara, imperfect bishtri. Final alif maqsura is a.
Palestinian passive with the it- prefix on the Form II stem of lagha: itlagha, غ as gh. Said of a cancelled appointment or flight.

Long uu in the stressed syllable and the feminine nisba ending -iyye, taa marbuta as e after ي.

The medial hamza is pronounced and written ': sa'al, imperfect bis'al. Also used for asking after someone.
English loan taken in with a long oo: shoort. Singular in Arabic even though English has the plural.
CiCiC stative past with ق as a glottal stop: zihi', imperfect yizha'. The participle zah'aan 'bored, fed up' is heard even more often.
خ is kh and the vowel is ee, not ii: kheeme, taa marbuta as e after م. Plural khiyam.
Said in Ramallah with a long ee, so I respell معلش as مَعْلِيش. ma fii is 'there isn't', the normal shop reply for something out of stock.
Form III feminine imperative with the short vowel dropped after the long aa: saam7iini, ح as 7, plus the object -ni.
The far feminine demonstrative in Palestinian, hadiik with long ii, beside haydiik. Masculine hadaak.
ظ is written TH per the scheme, realised in Ramallah as an emphatic z. Taa marbuta after ر is a. Entirely everyday vocabulary here.
The first short vowel drops, leaving an initial cluster: rfii3, with ع as 3. Of a thread, a slice or a line rather than a slim person, who is rfii3 or n7iif.
Palestinian participle prefix mit-, medial hamza written ', shadda doubling ك; the feminine ending drags the vowel out of the last syllable: mit'akkde. The question mark is not romanized.
il- assimilates to the sun letter س, and taa marbuta after ع is a. For the hour, Palestinians use the feminine tinteen, which I respell تِنْتِين since ث is t.
ط is a sun letter and emphatic, doubled whole: iT-Tayyaara, the Palestinian word for an aeroplane. The feminine participle loses its final short vowel: mit'akhkhra.
ظ is TH in the scheme, doubled by the shadda and said as an emphatic z in Ramallah. Mostly a label word; in the house people name the product or say Saabuun.
Form VII past with glottal ق and emphatic ط, plus the feminine -at before a following noun. kahraba ends in a long a in Palestinian; raa7at il-kahraba is the commoner way of saying it.
English loan with long ii: jiinz, used as a singular, as in banTaloon jiinz.
